text:
laura: Quick heads-up — while reviewing the generate API examples I spotted three issues: the request example shows "stream" as a string, the response sample omits the X-Request-Id header, and the Python SDK snippet still uses "max_tokens" instead of "max_new_tokens". Should I open a docs PR?

sam: Thanks for catching that. Can you paste the exact problematic snippets so we can triage?

laura: Sure — here's what I found:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/gpt-rc",
  "prompt": "Summarize...",
  "stream": "true",  // <-- should be boolean
  "max_tokens": 100    // <-- runtime uses max_new_tokens now
}
```
And the response example just shows the JSON body (200) but doesn't show the X-Request-Id header that the API actually returns.

jordan: Oof, nice catches. OpenAPI schema defines stream: boolean. Our examples linter didn't catch it because some examples are freeform. Also the SDK migration renamed max_tokens -> max_new_tokens in the last release, so docs lagging.

devex-bot: PR template created: docs PR draft #3345 (docs/generate-examples-fix). CI note: examples-lint ran and flagged type mismatch in docs/examples/generate.md.

laura: I'll update the examples and the Python snippet. Quick question: for the X-Request-Id, should we surface it as "X-Request-Id: <uuid>" in the response sample headers, or also add a "request_id" field to the JSON body?

mike: We return it as a response header (X-Request-Id). Historically we only included it in the body for a few legacy examples, which confused people. I'd prefer showing the header explicitly and call out that it's available for tracing.

sam: Agree with mike. Show the header in the sample HTTP response and add a one-line note in the example text: "The service also returns X-Request-Id header for tracing." Also add a migration note for max_new_tokens rename.

jordan: Small extra: JS SDK snippet in the docs currently uses client.generate(...). Our JS SDK surface is client.chat.generate(...) for chat/generate dual examples. Make sure both Python and JS snippets are updated and consistent.

laura: Good catch — will update both. I'll also run the docs typecheck script locally (scripts/validate_examples.py) to catch the string-vs-boolean before pushing.

devex-bot: PR #3345 opened by laura: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3345 — CI: examples-lint ✅, linkcheck ✅, typecheck ❌ (fails on sample typing).

mike: If typecheck still fails after you change the example, run `python scripts/validate_examples.py docs/examples/generate.md` and paste output here if it still fails. I can help iterate.

laura: Will do. Assigning the PR to myself, adding a changelog note and a short migration blurb about max_tokens -> max_new_tokens. I'll ping when CI is green.

sam: Awesome — once green we can merge and cherry-pick to release branch. Thanks laura! :shipit:

laura: Thanks all, pushing updates now.
